nodes.text: A diffusion probabilistic model is a parameterized Markov chain trained by variational inference whose learned Gaussian reverse transitions reverse a fixed forward Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to data.
nodes.evidence: A diffusion probabilistic model... is a parameterized Markov chain trained using variational inference to produce samples matching the data after finite time

nodes.text: A particular epsilon-prediction parameterization of diffusion models reveals an equivalence between training and denoising score matching over multiple noise levels, and between sampling and annealed Langevin dynamics; the authors consider this equivalence a primary contribution.
nodes.evidence: a certain parameterization of diffusion models reveals an equivalence with denoising score matching over multiple noise levels during training and with annealed Langevin dynamics during sampling... we consider this equivalence to be one of our primary contributions

nodes.text: Instead of predicting the posterior mean, the reverse process predicts the added noise epsilon, yielding a simplified unweighted mean-squared-error training objective (L_simple) that resembles denoising score matching.
nodes.evidence: Lsimple(θ) := Et,x0, − θ( α¯tx0 + 1 − α¯t , t) 2

nodes.text: The forward process admits closed-form sampling of x_t at any timestep via q(x_t|x_0)=N(x_t; sqrt(alpha_bar_t) x_0, (1-alpha_bar_t) I), enabling efficient stochastic-gradient training on random terms.
nodes.evidence: q(xt|x0) = N (xt; α¯tx0, (1 − α¯t)I)... Efficient training is therefore possible by optimizing random terms of L with stochastic gradient descent

nodes.text: The simplified objective is a weighted variational bound that down-weights small-t terms (small-noise denoising), letting the network focus on harder large-t denoising and yielding better sample quality than the true variational bound.
nodes.evidence: the simplified objective to down-weight loss terms corresponding to small t... this reweighting leads to better sample quality

nodes.text: The sampling procedure is a type of progressive lossy decoding that resembles and vastly generalizes autoregressive decoding along a bit ordering.
nodes.evidence: the sampling procedure of diffusion models is a type of progressive decoding that resembles autoregressive decoding along a bit ordering that vastly generalizes what is normally possible with autoregressive models

nodes.text: On unconditional CIFAR10 the model achieves an Inception score of 9.46 and a state-of-the-art FID of 3.17, with sample quality better than most models in the literature including class-conditional ones.
nodes.evidence: On the unconditional CIFAR10 dataset, we obtain an Inception score of 9.46 and a state-of-the-art FID score of 3.17

nodes.text: On 256x256 LSUN the model obtains sample quality similar to ProgressiveGAN (LSUN Church FID=7.89, Bedroom FID=4.90).
nodes.evidence: On 256x256 LSUN, we obtain sample quality similar to ProgressiveGAN

nodes.text: Training on the true variational bound yields better codelengths (NLL) than the simplified objective, but the simplified objective yields the best sample quality; the models do not have competitive log likelihoods versus other likelihood-based models.
nodes.evidence: training our models on the true variational bound yields better codelengths than training on the simplified objective, as expected, but the latter yields the best sample quality

nodes.text: The majority of the models' lossless codelengths are consumed describing imperceptible image details, interpreted via lossy compression.
nodes.evidence: the majority of our models' lossless codelengths are consumed to describe imperceptible image details

nodes.text: Implementation uses a U-Net backbone resembling PixelCNN++ with group normalization, parameters shared across time via Transformer sinusoidal position embeddings, and self-attention at 16x16 resolution, with T=1000 and linearly increasing variances from 1e-4 to 0.02.
nodes.evidence: we use a U-Net backbone similar to an unmasked PixelCNN++ with group normalization... Transformer sinusoidal position embedding... self-attention at the 16 × 16 feature map resolution

nodes.text: KL divergences in the variance-reduced variational bound are comparisons between Gaussians using tractable forward-process posteriors conditioned on x_0, allowing closed-form Rao-Blackwellized computation instead of high-variance Monte Carlo.
nodes.evidence: all KL divergences in Eq. (5) are comparisons between Gaussians, so they can be calculated in a Rao-Blackwellized fashion with closed form expressions
